verdict.rationale: PayPal's ACP path uses a delegated, one-time-use Braintree token that is bound to the merchant ID and carries configurable amount and time restrictions, and the UCP path likewise delivers a single-use tokenized credential instead of raw card data. However, PayPal documents this from the merchant-acceptance side: the token is minted through ChatGPT or Google Pay, and the restrictions are configured by the merchant, not by the user handing the credential to an agent. Missing for 10: user-facing issuance and configuration of scoped credentials, user-set spending limits/expiry/merchant allow-lists, multi-use bounded credentials beyond single-use tokens, independent or hands-on corroboration.
